title: Run admission and target occupancy
summary: Source and containment preparation precede bounded item/run locks; locked validation rereads mutable facts and reuses only identical repository answers. Open lane heads ask no repository question; a new question (such as an item landing meanwhile) is answered with locks released and the locked phase retried, up to eight preparations, before the start refuses naming the exact source key. A run before its first QA stage occupies its origins as deploying, whatever its QA owes, so a memberless run cannot be overwritten mid-deploy. Occupancy shares QA facts within one evaluation and stops at its first blocker. Item or run-level QA followed by gates and final auto completion permits takeover; execution work, different flow/target, missing containment, another live driver, or a covering steering seat the caller neither holds nor created the older run under prevents it. Refusals name the actual facts; recreating alone is not recovery. Structured run reads preserve complete preparation receipts, including shell pipes in member instructions, for exact-request recovery after response loss. Every admission (carried enrollment, takeover, creation and add-item) reads bindings, completion flows, intake and snapshot inputs once for the whole member set, locks requirements and plans in ID order, inserts every row in one statement, and discards mutable inputs before the next composition pass; takeover transfers its QA records and moving membership in set-based writes and the executing transition validates and freezes every member in set reads and one write, so none of them grows with the member count. Canonical member validation and atomic takeover remain authoritative. Ordinary removal retains its orphan/retraction checks; takeover does not use removal cleanup for preserved work. Failed successors retaining inherited QA can retry or transfer it again; they remain failed until normal recovery succeeds. Existing timing records distinguish provisional composition, locked composition, enrollment, commit and response reads; aggregate durations do not prove an individual loop caused latency. Carried enrollment stops at the first item it cannot admit; the omission refusal then names that item and its cause.
